description:
User approved 2026-11-18, verbatim via GC: "agreed; proceed". The plan is page v4: https://claude.ai/artifact/BB1FpQ1Cf7Jd5spZeLEWtg (From: GC). It replaces 'block ages first'. Ideal assembly comes first: steps C0-C7 make the collector's hot paths the hand-written sequence, and the policy round (step P) comes last. Each child is one commit, judged on bench. Builder: GC.

Previous description, kept for step P:
fz promotes every survivor of a collection to old blocks (retire_to_space_as_old, runtime/src/heap/imp.rs) and a major leaves every survivor old. OTP promotes only the mature part of the young heap, below the high-water mark, which already survived one minor (erl_gc.c:1436, 1819), and a fullsweep leaves its survivors young with bin_old_vheap = 0 (erl_gc.c:1954, 3292-3295). Found by the fz-9x7.8 post-mortem (https://claude.ai/artifact/PQXu69Go2gfWdLDfSkoxrW): survive's per-round binaries are live at one minor, become old, and wait for a heap-driven major (72 MB dead).
Design (approved page https://claude.ai/artifact/PC7vJ3veeQqqQca2ppEnWp): three block ages fresh / mature / old; a minor's from-space is fresh + mature; a survivor moves up one age; writes in place stay fresh-only; binary and resource stubs get a mature chain; live_baseline = mature + old; gc event gains mature_bytes and old_bytes.
Experiment first (pre-registered on the page): per-variant release builds V0 / A1 (major places by the same rule) / A2 (OTP: major leaves all survivors mature) / A1G / A2G (gifts grafted mature), round 5's 17 workloads, 9 interleaved runs; rule: survive RSS falls >= 25%, instruction and RSS guards on every workload; lowest geomean instructions among passing variants is built.

comments.text: Stays open: re-test as the collector is cleaned up; ageing is not discarded on one bad round. Record so far: A1 (own source) failed rounds 2-3; part of round 3's enum cost was forward_heap_value being out of line, which fz-nml.22 (#675) now inlines. A2 / A1G / A2G were NEVER measured: they were selected by build-time env, which fz2's build.rs does not rebuild the AOT runtime archive for, so each linked A1's archive (round 3 A1h/A2h held ratios identical to 3 decimals on all 17 workloads). Next round: per-arm runtime archives (FZ_AOT_RUNTIME_STATICLIB), rebased onto develop including #675 and whatever wins fz-9x7.14/.15.

Round 4 (bench, develop 2c4641f52 incl #675, per-arm runtime archives so A2/A1G/A2G are measured for the first time; 25 runs/arm, 9 dist-full; outputs identical): all four arms FAIL round 3's rule. Rule 1 (survive held falls >=25%) fails everywhere: survive held 1.286 (A1/A1G), 1.324 (A2/A2G). Cycles: A1 enum 1.096 (round 3: 1.225, so #675 removed about half the gap), dist-p28000 1.069, dist-full 1.059, survive 1.049; A2 is costlier on every allocation-heavy workload (enum 1.191, dist 1.14, qsort 1.074) and its held rises on fanin/qsort/dist (dist-full 1.695); G variants add fanin 1.28 / ring 1.16 / msg 1.07 and cut held on ring/msg (0.31/0.38). Stays open per the user.

2026-11-17 collection counts vs BEAM (OTP 28, per-process gc trace of the workload's own processes, scratchpad/beam/gctrace.exs; BEAM's harness floor is ~25 minor / 10 major, seen on spin). fz develop minor/major vs BEAM: msg 68,833/25,324 vs 8,079/11; ring 55,281/7,888 vs 18/10; reqrep 1/20,001 vs 14,850/14; maps 212/107 vs 600/23; survive 6/4 (.8: 19/4) vs 122/29. Mechanisms: (1) every minor promotes everything it copies, so the old bytes double past a 512 B reference within a few minors on small processes and majors fire constantly (msg 27% majors, reqrep 100%); (2) young budget = live bytes floored at 512 B (BEAM min heap 233 words = 1,864 B), checked at every park, so msg/ring collect every ~1 KB (fz-9x7.7). Earlier rounds judged survive held and instructions only; collection counts against BEAM are a direct signal for this ticket's next round. The .8 old-binary major fold (survive mean 0.80x but instructions 1.144x) addresses the same survive mechanism this ticket describes.
User ruling 2026-11-17: the next round's rule adds collection counts (minor/major) against BEAM's, measured with scratchpad/beam/gctrace.exs.

Input (Make Distiller Fast session's profile, bench, develop 2eff1dec2, 1,498 samples, one run; bench:distill-hunt/prof.j.base.txt): collection is 15.4% of the distiller. Samples: memmove 70, cheney_scan 48, cheney_forward_object 43, strict_object_size 26, forward_heap_value 25. Predates fz-9x7.38 (forward_heap_value inline(always)).
User ruling 2026-11-18 (relayed by GC): a fresh look; earlier arms (A1/A2/A1G/A2G) were measured on bases since changed (#719, #722, #731, #735). GC starts it.

Input (MDF bench profile, develop 37c5473cd, 5 runs): collector 13.6% inclusive of the distiller; memmove under cheney_forward_object 4.2%; heap_object_word 2.4% self and AnyValue::decode_parts 2.3% self as out-of-line calls from cheney_scan (any_value.rs:365/518/573 carry no #[inline]; only the free fn at :897 does). Per-byte trace cost, independent of the round-5 arms.

title: The collector runs the hand-written sequence, then its policy round
